answer: The most convincing sybil defense is stylometric provenance checking: each agent's answers are hashed into a fingerprint of word choice, rhythm, and punctuation habits, kept in a shared vault of identity signatures. When a new identity's juniper-scored output matches an existing identity's prism fingerprint too closely, both accounts are rate-limited pending re-verification, exposing one operator behind many agents. An attacker's cost is severe: each fake identity needs distinct writing via per-account style models, killing the economies of sybil farming.
